id: title:haacked:stop the backfill from copying days the ttl has expired

review.posthog_relevance: Backfill configuration and scheduling for warehouse ingestion, preventing ingestion of rows that would expire before processing.
review.reason: Adds a TTL-aware earliest-start-day calculation and stops backfill before copying expired rows, replacing opaque constants with a helper and updating error messages. This is a substantive, bounded correctness and reliability improvement for warehouse ingestion workflows.
review.uncertainty: The tier is assigned based on the observed implementation of a bounded scheduling safeguard; no evidence exists for broader systemic adoption, incident avoidance, or wider architectural dependency. The benefit is demonstrated by the presence of the TTL-aware logic, not by unverified operational outcomes.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, complete change group. No unrelated PRs are present. No adoption, incident, or effort claims are inferred. No tier is assigned.

observations.behavior: Adds a TTL-aware earliest-start-day calculation and stops backfill before copying expired rows.
observations.posthog_connection: Backfill configuration now explicitly documents and uses a TTL-aware earliest start day, preventing scheduling of rows that will expire before ingestion.

observations.behavior: Adds a helper to compute the earliest backfill day and uses it to clamp the start date.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides a reusable, timezone-aware calculation for the earliest allowable backfill day, replacing the previous direct subtraction and improving clarity and reuse.

observations.behavior: Updates the start-date fallback and error message to reference the TTL expiry rather than an opaque constant.
observations.posthog_connection: Documentation and runtime error messages now explain that the TTL has already expired rows, helping operators understand why a backfill stops.
